statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-58160 (GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5, RUSTSEC-2025-0055): tracing-subscriber before 0.3.20 writes logged values to the terminal without escaping ANSI escape sequences, so untrusted text that reaches a log message can change what the terminal shows. It is fixed in 0.3.20 by commit 4c52ca5, which adds escaping to the formatter (fmt/format/escape.rs): https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing/security/advisories/GHSA-xwfj-jgwm-7wp5, https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0055.html, https://github.com/tokio-rs/tracing/commit/4c52ca5266a3920fc5dfeebda2accf15ee7fb278. Scanned every file of every package of this owner published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: all 17 packages (rust, cargo, rustc-dev, rustfmt, rust-clippy, rust-dbg, rust-src, rust-wasm, rust-uefi, rust-gdb, rust-lldb and the doc and completion packages) of builds 1.91.1-r0, 1.91.1-r3 and 1.91.1-r4, and build 1.91.1-r2, which publishes only rust and cargo. The compiler library /usr/lib/librustc_driver-*.so in the rust package of every one of those builds is compiled with tracing-subscriber 0.3.18, as are /usr/bin/rustfmt and /usr/bin/rustdoc in builds 1.91.1-r0, -r3 and -r4, and rustc-dev ships that crate's 0.3.18 compiled metadata for compiler extensions. The published debug symbols (rust-dbg, x86_64, 1.91.1-r0, -r3 and -r4) show that librustc_driver and rustfmt contain tracing-subscriber's default field formatter and none of the escaping code the fix adds. cargo is compiled with tracing-subscriber 0.3.20, which carries the fix. No published build of this owner has a fixed copy in the compiler, so every published build is affected.
